title: Conormal modules of compatible ideals commute with filtered colimits
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $J$ a small filtered category, and $P:J\to\operatorname{CAlg}_R$ a diagram of commutative $R$-algebras with colimit cocone $(P_\infty,(p_j))$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $I_j\subseteq P_j$ be ideals satisfying $P(a)(I_j)\subseteq I_k$ for every arrow $a:j\to k$. Let $I\subseteq P_\infty$ be an ideal such that $p_j(I_j)\subseteq I$ for every $j$ and every $x\in I$ equals $p_j(x_j)$ for some $j$ and $x_j\in I_j$. For an ideal $L$ of a commutative ring $B$, let $L^2$ denote the ideal of finite sums of products of two elements of $L$, and let $L/L^2$ be the quotient of the additive $R$-module $L$ by its submodule $L^2$, with scalars restricted along $R\to B$. Give $j\mapsto I_j/I_j^2$ the transition maps $[x]\mapsto[P(a)(x)]$. Then the $R$-linear maps $q_j:I_j/I_j^2\to I/I^2$, $[x]\mapsto[p_j(x)]$, exhibit $I/I^2$ as the colimit in $R$-modules of this diagram [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. No injectivity, flatness or finite-generation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 07BQ (lemma-colimits-NL), proof: general ideal-square quotient argument implicit after the identification of the kernel as a filtered colimit.

proof.text: An $R$-algebra homomorphism carrying an ideal $L$ into an ideal $L\prime$ carries $\sum_{r=1}^n a_rb_r$, with $a_r,b_r\in L$, to $\sum_{r=1}^n f(a_r)f(b_r)\in (L\prime)^2$. Its restriction to $L$ is $R$-linear and therefore induces an $R$-linear map on the quotients by the squares. Apply this to each $P(a)$ and $p_j$. The identity and composition laws, and $q_k\circ M(a)=q_j$ for $M_j=I_j/I_j^2$, hold on each representative $[x]$, by the corresponding laws for $P$ and its colimit cocone. Thus the displayed quotient maps form a diagram and a cocone.

source.place: Tag 07BQ (lemma-colimits-NL), proof, ideal-square quotient step expanded by a finite-products argument.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise](1), $(P_\infty,(p_j))$ is also a colimit of the underlying commutative rings. Hence [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise](2) applies: equality of images of any two ring elements can be witnessed after two arrows to a common object. Here the indexing category is precisely the given small filtered $J$; no change of index category is being made.

source.place: Tag 07BQ (lemma-colimits-NL), proof, ideal-square quotient step expanded by a finite-products argument.

proof.text: Every element of $I/I^2$ has a representative $x\in I$. By the hypothesis on $I$, choose $j$ and $x_j\in I_j$ with $p_j(x_j)=x$. Then its class is $q_j([x_j])$. This verifies joint surjectivity of the cocone on underlying sets.

source.place: Tag 07BQ (lemma-colimits-NL), proof, ideal-square quotient step expanded by a finite-products argument.

proof.text: Fix $j$ and a class $z=[x]\in I_j/I_j^2$ with $q_j(z)=0$. Then $p_j(x)\in I^2$, so by the stated definition write $p_j(x)=\sum_{r=1}^n a_rb_r$, with $a_r,b_r\in I$. Lift each factor to an element of some $I_i$ using the hypothesis on $I$. There are only finitely many such indices. Repeatedly use the common-object clause of filteredness [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] to choose one object $t$, an arrow $u:j\to t$, and arrows from all these factor indices to $t$. Their images $A_r,B_r$ belong to $I_t$ by compatibility of the ideals. Put $X=P(u)(x)$ and $Y=\sum_r A_rB_r\in I_t^2$. The cocone identities and preservation of sums and products give $p_t(X)=p_j(x)=p_t(Y)$. If $n=0$, take $t=j$, $u=\mathrm{id}_j$, and $Y=0$; thus this argument also covers a relation with no products.

source.place: Tag 07BQ (lemma-colimits-NL), proof, ideal-square quotient step expanded by a finite-products argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise](2) to $X,Y\in P_t$ and the ring colimit from step 2. Obtain arrows $v,w:t\to k$ with $P(v)(X)=P(w)(Y)$. The parallel-arrow clause of filteredness [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $e:k\to l$ with $e\circ v=e\circ w$. Set $h=e\circ v=e\circ w$. Applying $P(e)$ to the equality yields $P(h)(X)=P(h)(Y)$. Since $Y\in I_t^2$, its image is a sum of products of elements of $I_l$, hence belongs to $I_l^2$. Therefore the single arrow $h\circ u:j\to l$ sends $z$ to zero in $I_l/I_l^2$. This proves eventual vanishing of every class in the kernel of $q_j$, even when the original transition maps have kernels.

source.place: Tag 07BQ (lemma-colimits-NL), proof, ideal-square quotient step expanded by a finite-products argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-criterion] to the small filtered category $J$, the $R$-module diagram $M_j=I_j/I_j^2$, and the cocone with vertex $I/I^2$ from step 1. Its first hypothesis is step 3, and its equivalent kernel-vanishing second hypothesis is steps 4 and 5. It concludes that this very cocone is a colimit in $R$-modules, with the prescribed maps $q_j$. All constructions used only compatibility and the stated lifting property of $I$, so no injectivity, flatness or finite generation is required.
